findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py: `rebound = _rebind_sequential(...)` runs before `_sequential_round`. template/scripts/orchestrate_pre_authoring.py: `_affected_sources` always seeds from `_file_sources(add_document)`, even when `remaining_changes` is empty. Skipping the rebind once every child is Done, or restricting the affected set to the remaining children's specs when none remain, would avoid it.
findings.summary: For a sequential Requirement, advance calls `_rebind_sequential` on every pass while pre-authoring is not complete. That includes the pass after the last child is Done, when no child remains. The affected-source set still includes the ADD's file evidence and reused constraints. A foreign commit on one of those files can therefore raise RebindStop and block the retrospective or terminal step. It would not be reported as the pending-retrospective next step, which contradicts outcome 3 in that case.

tests/test_requirement_execution.py now patches `execution._retrospective_pending` to return None for every test in the class. The existing coverage of the real `require_checkpoint` call path from advance (single-child, shared-candidate and terminal branches) is therefore bypassed. The new housekeeping tests cover the pending-status behavior only partly.
